Euthanasia (Biblical Doctrine)
yoo-thuh-NAY-zhuh
noun (Christian ethics)
From Greek eu (good) + thanatos (death): the deliberate killing of a person to end suffering, whether by direct action (active euthanasia) or by deliberate withholding of ordinary care (passive euthanasia). The biblical-ethical doctrine holds that the deliberate killing of an innocent person, including for the relief of suffering, is murder forbidden by the sixth commandment.

📖 Biblical Definition

From Greek eu (good) + thanatos (death): the deliberate killing of a person to end suffering. Distinguished into (1) active euthanasia (direct killing, e.g., lethal injection); (2) passive euthanasia (deliberate withholding of ordinary care with the intention of causing death); and (3) physician-assisted suicide (the physician provides the means for the patient to kill himself). The biblical-ethical doctrine holds that the deliberate killing of an innocent person, including for the relief of suffering, is murder forbidden by the sixth commandment (Exodus 20:13). The biblical foundation: (1) human life is the gift of God, not the possession of the individual to dispose of at will (Job 1:21, the LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; Deuteronomy 32:39, I kill, and I make alive); (2) the deliberate killing of the innocent is murder (Exodus 20:13; Genesis 9:6); (3) suffering, while real and grievous, does not justify the taking of innocent life, and the Christian's response to suffering is the substantive ministry of presence, palliative care, and gospel hope (2 Corinthians 1:3-7; Romans 8:18). The Reformed-confessional ethic distinguishes the deliberate killing of a patient (euthanasia, forbidden) from the legitimate withholding or withdrawal of extraordinary or futile medical interventions when death is imminent and the interventions only prolong the dying process (which is not euthanasia but the acceptance of death's approach). The patriarchal-Reformed reader holds the substantive biblical doctrine: euthanasia and physician-assisted suicide are forms of murder or suicide forbidden by Scripture; the church is called to oppose them, to provide substantive care for the suffering and dying, and to proclaim the gospel hope that transforms the Christian's experience of suffering and death.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The deliberate killing of a person to end suffering (active, passive, or physician-assisted); biblical doctrine holds it murder/suicide forbidden by the sixth commandment; life is God's gift not the individual's to dispose of (Job 1:21; Deuteronomy 32:39); distinguished from legitimate withholding of futile interventions.

EUTHANASIA (BIBLICAL DOCTRINE), n. (Christian ethics; Greek eu [good] + thanatos [death]) The deliberate killing of a person to end suffering. Forms: active (direct killing), passive (deliberate withholding of ordinary care to cause death), physician-assisted suicide. Biblical doctrine: deliberate killing of the innocent, including for relief of suffering, is murder (Exodus 20:13). Foundation: (1) life is God's gift, not the individual's to dispose of (Job 1:21; Deuteronomy 32:39); (2) killing the innocent is murder (Genesis 9:6); (3) suffering does not justify taking innocent life; Christian response is ministry of presence, palliative care, gospel hope. Distinguished from legitimate withholding of extraordinary/futile interventions when death is imminent.

📖 Key Scripture

Exodus 20:13 — "Thou shalt not kill."

Job 1:21 — "And said, Naked came I out of my mother's womb, and naked shall I return thither: the LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD."

Deuteronomy 32:39 — "See now that I, even I, am he, and there is no god with me: I kill, and I make alive; I wound, and I heal: neither is there any that can deliver out of my hand."

2 Corinthians 1:3-4 — "Blessed be God, even the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort; Who comforteth us in all our tribulation, that we may be able to comfort them which are in any trouble."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The pro-euthanasia position (the individual has a right to die; suffering justifies killing) contradicts the biblical doctrine that life is God's gift; euthanasia and physician-assisted suicide are forms of murder or suicide.

expand to see more

The contemporary pro-euthanasia position (the individual has a right to die; the relief of suffering justifies the killing of the suffering person; death-with-dignity requires the option of assisted suicide) contradicts the biblical doctrine. Human life is the gift of God, not the possession of the individual to dispose of at will: the LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away (Job 1:21); I kill, and I make alive (Deuteronomy 32:39). The timing and manner of death belong to the LORD, not to the individual or the physician. Suffering, while real and grievous, does not justify the killing of innocent life; the Christian's response to suffering is the substantive ministry of presence, palliative care, and gospel hope, not the lethal shortcut of euthanasia. The patriarchal-Reformed reader distinguishes carefully: euthanasia (the deliberate killing of the patient) is forbidden; the legitimate withholding or withdrawal of extraordinary or futile medical interventions when death is imminent (which accepts the approach of death without deliberately causing it) is not euthanasia and is morally permissible. The church's calling is to oppose euthanasia and assisted suicide, to provide substantive care for the suffering and dying, and to proclaim the gospel hope that transforms the Christian's experience of death from terror into the gate of glory.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek eu + thanatos; life as God's gift (Job 1:21; Deuteronomy 32:39); sixth commandment; distinguished from withholding futile interventions.
